title: Vaccination against COVID-19, Influenza, and Pneumococcal Disease in the Elderly
summary:
As people age, the immune system becomes weaker, and infections such as influenza, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), and pneumococcal disease can take a more severe course. Vaccinations are intended to provide protection, but it is still partly unclear how effective they are in older age and across different seasons.

In this study, patients aged 60 years and older who are hospitalized with a respiratory infection are asked to complete a questionnaire about their current symptoms and possible pre-existing conditions. In addition, vaccination status against respiratory pathogens is recorded. The aim is to determine how well vaccinations protect older adults from severe respiratory diseases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Hospitalization, sufficient knowledge of German, informed consent, positive test for exactly one (case) or none (control) of the pathogens under investigation (SARS-CoV-2, influenza virus, pneumococci), negative RSV test
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of ability to provide informed consent, palliative treatment (life expectancy <72h), prior enrollment in the present study, transfer from another hospital facility (except in the case of pneumococcal infection)
